Tips for using this phrasebook

  • Say the English first if you are unsure, then point to the line. A smile and a slow pace do more than perfect grammar.
  • The small line under each phrase is a rough pronunciation guide, not a precise phonetic transcription. Stress the capitalized syllables in Spanish.
  • Arabic is written right to left. The Arabic column is set with RTL direction so the script reads correctly; the romanization under it stays left to right.
  • Japanese forms here are polite everyday speech. Adding お願いします (onegaishimasu) or ください (kudasai) keeps requests soft.
  • Hindi and Arabic greetings and “please” vary by region and formality. These are widely understood travel forms, not the only correct ones.
  • For medical or safety phrases, show the written line as well as speaking it. Numbers, allergies, and place names are safer written down.

Twenty phrases across four groups. Spellings follow common travel usage; local accents will differ.
